head: A ready-to-paste set of descriptions, a what's-new list since v26, features, a naming guide, a getting-started guide and posts for Guyanonymous' Wildcards v43 (built to celebrate global diversity, can only make adult characters).
intro: The library has grown from printed T-shirts and uniforms into a full wardrobe, accessory, scene and overlay system. Here is what each stretch added, newest first.

Version 73

Expressions have intensity now. 68 emotions come in mild, strong and extreme tiers, each described by what the mouth, eyes, brows and head do, with the emotion name kept as a label. Both expression files were rebuilt from them, and expr_mild, expr_strong and expr_extreme let you pick the intensity yourself.

A consistency pass over the scene entry points. City time and weather are drawn as matching pairs, penguins and flightless birds never fly, clothing condition prompts no longer mix a spotless item with broken fastenings, and a check script flags such pairs (182 flagged before, 0 to 1 after).
A depth and occlusion family (depth_*) for choosing who or what is in front of whom, with a scale rule (far figures about one third the height of near ones) taken from the 16-person scene tests.
Anchoring phase 2. 6,568 sentences in 448 long-form person files now start with 'The woman's', 'The man's' or 'The person's' instead of Her, His or Their.

Cleanup. 272 file names with a double underscore were renamed and every reference fixed, blank padding in mark_tattoo and dem_unique became single-space none options, curly quotes, dashes and a colon were removed, school-backpack wording was reworded, and a general chastity_belt group was added.

New tools. check_build.py is a standing check before every release, and the All Options Once builder now builds safely into a temporary folder, finds its modules by itself and refuses to replace the real folder after a failed run.
Version 72

Facial hair is now described, not named. Image tests showed that style names such as soul patch, balbo beard or Van Dyke are unreliable, and a shaved face often came out with a white beard. All 303 distinct lines in `m_facial_hair`, the nine `m_age<lo>_<hi>_facial_hair` files and the nine `any_age<lo>_<hi>_facial_hair` files now say where the hair grows, where the skin is bare, and how long and how shaped it is. The soul patch is a tiny tuft of hair directly under the lower lip about the size of a thumbprint, and shaved faces use positive wording (smooth, shiny, hairless skin on the chin, cheeks and upper lip, like freshly shaved skin). Line counts and age weights are unchanged.
The person templates now say `His lower face has ...` or `Their lower face has ...` instead of `facial hair is`, so hair lines and bare-skin lines both read correctly.

Scar lines describe how the scar looks. The 398 generated lines in `mark_scars` and `skin_scars` (a shape word plus a body place) now give colour, relief and length, for example a thin, pale, slightly raised scar about four centimetres long on the forearm. The same short wording had drawn a pale raised scar in one image and a deep shadow-filled one in another. Hand-written scar lines are unchanged.

The anchor pass from the build called v71 is included. Furniture descriptions that started a sentence with `It has` are merged into one `The <object> has A, B and C` sentence, room openers use the room noun, the person templates (`m_`, `f_` and `any_` create_random files and `world_c_` files) are one chained sentence per person with no pronoun-start sentences, the ageing summary pieces start with `The man`, `The woman` or `This person`, and six bare `none` furniture options are reworded. The reason is that in a scene with several people the model mixes up attributes when a sentence starts with `He` or `She`.

The scripts that make these changes (`_tools/v71_build.py`, `_tools/v72_facial_hair.py`, `_tools/v72_scars.py`) are in the `_tools` folder. Run them in that order after any rebuild. Each can be undone with `--restore`.

104 real manufacturers and makers across 10 categories (43 car makers, 15 motorcycle makers, 11 truck, bus and tractor makers, 9 aircraft makers, 8 bicycle makers, 5 skateboard and skate styles, 4 boat builders, 4 rail and bus styles, 3 space programmes, 2 scooter makers), with 213 decade descriptions from the 1930s to the 2020s.

This is the one part of the library that uses real brand names on purpose, as you asked. Each style is also described in plain visual terms (grille shape, roofline, lamps, fins, stripes, tank shape and so on), so it works even when a model does not know the name.

Per maker: `maker_<maker>_<decade>` (one decade), `maker_<maker>_style` (any decade), `maker_<maker>_genre` (the vehicle genres it makes, taken from the v69 genres and described without a random paint job so the maker's own look decides the colours and details), and the entries `maker_<maker>_prompt`, `maker_<maker>_scene_prompt` (with a pose and camera angle) and `maker_<maker>_person_prompt` (with a person). `maker_<maker>_<decade>_prompt` pins a decade.

Mix and entry files. `maker_prompt`, `maker_scene_prompt` and `maker_person_prompt` pick any maker. `maker_<category>_prompt` picks within cars, trucks, motorcycles, scooters, bicycles, boats, aircraft, spacecraft, rail or skates. `maker_decade_<decade>_prompt` and `maker_decade_prompt` pick by decade. `maker_blend_prompt` blends two makers' styles on a random real vehicle, and `maker_style_any` can be dropped into any vehicle prompt.
The index `docs/MAKERS_v70.txt` lists every maker, the genres it applies to and the decades covered.

157 vehicle genres in 9 domains. Road (24: city car to supercar, muscle car, hot rod, rally car, race car, limousine, microcar, lowrider, art car, taxi, police car), trucks (12), two-wheelers and skates (30: cruisers to dirt bikes, road to cargo bicycles, kick and electric scooters, unicycle, skateboard, longboard, roller skates, inline skates), rail (10), working and leisure vehicles (16: tractors, harvesters, forklifts, carriages, wagons, sleighs, campers, caravans, buses), watercraft (26), aircraft (16), spacecraft (8) and imagined vehicles (15: flying cars, hoverbikes, steampunk airships, mechs, sky galleons, starships, flying carpets, clockwork carriages and more).

Every genre is built in parts: `vx_<genre>_form`, `_feature` and `_setting`, assembled by `vx_<genre>_prompt` with the paintwork from the paint system. Each prompt starts with a plain explanation of what the vehicle is.

Poses and states. Eleven vehicle classes (car, truck, motorbike, bicycle, skate, rail, boat, ship, air, space, imagined) each have `vs_<class>_state` (wheels turned, lights on or off, doors, bonnet or boot open, drifting, parked, covered, on a jack, heeled over, taking off and more), `vs_<class>_camera` (angles) and `vs_special_<genre>` for 49 specialised vehicles (tipping dump truck, extended fire ladder, winching tow truck, hovering helicopter, inflating balloon, lifting-off rocket and more).

People with vehicles. `vs_<class>_person` has poses for one person using or touching the vehicle (hands at the wheel, kneeling at a tyre, looking under the bonnet, changing a wheel, leaning on the door, leaning into a bend, coiling a rope, climbing into a cockpit) and `vs_<class>_group` has poses for groups (a pit crew, a family loading the boot, riders side by side, a ground crew). `vx_<genre>_person_prompt`, `_group_prompt` and `_person_frame_prompt` put them together, with the v57 full-body framing for people.

Paint. `vpaint_colour` (40 named shades), `vpaint_finish` (17 finishes from gloss and metallic flake to patina, chrome wrap and vinyl) and `vpaint_effect` (20 markings from racing stripes and flames to camouflage and sign-writing), combined in `vpaint_prompt` and `vpaint_scene_prompt`.

Damage. `vdmg_<class>_light`, `_moderate` and `_heavy` give wear, scratches, dents, cracked glass and wrecks for six classes. `vxd_<class>_prompt`, `vxd_prompt` and `vxd_ruined_prompt` apply them, and `vx_condition_prompt` links the v62 condition system.

Interiors and details. `vint_<class>_prompt` and `vint_prompt` give cabins, dashboards, seats, an open boot (empty or packed), engine bays, wheels and brakes, exhausts, chains and sprockets, underside of a deck, driver cabs, carriages, cockpits, galleys and flight decks, each with matching trim and materials.

Version 68

Condition parts fixed. The part lists for buildings, vehicles, furniture, clothing and statues in the v62 condition system were too specific (a bridge could get a damaged front door, a glove could get damaged sleeves). They now name parts that exist on every subject of that kind, such as entrance, stonework, wheels or running gear, legs or base, main fabric and plinth.

Sea animals fixed. Jellyfish, corals, anemones, starfish and urchins now have their own behaviour family (drifting with the current, waving tentacles, clinging to a rock) instead of sharing one with crabs and shellfish, so a jellyfish is never asked to burrow into sand.
Object condition prompts fixed. They now use tools only, because machines such as tractors belong to the vehicle kind and were being given handles.
World place prompts fixed. `world_<name>_place_prompt` now reads "Visible nearby are ..." so the sentence always starts correctly.
Also included: the full v57 to v67 gallery of 200 sample prompts, organised in groups, as a separate download.
Version 67

Nine effect domains, each with 8 to 10 effects written twice. The real tier is a physically plausible approximation (what could actually be photographed) and the spectacle tier is the film-style version. Both stay photographic, so an illustrative style from v62 translates cleanly. Domains: magic and spellwork, transformation (partial changes with swirling marks), belief-neutral miraculous and mythic events (parted waters, pillar of fire, staff to serpent and others), sacred light and atmosphere, science (arcs, plasma, lasers, bioluminescence, ferrofluid), cultural and secular (fireworks, lanterns, powder, drone shows), stage tricks and illusions, optical illusions, and atmosphere and light physics.

Effects are built from parts. `fx_<domain>_real` or `_spectacle` is what, `fx_where_<person|place|sky|object>` is where it sits, `fx_strength` is subtle, moderate or dramatic, `fx_colour_real` and `fx_colour_spectacle` are the light, and `fx_interact_<target>` says how it affects the scene.

Entry points. `fx_<domain>_real_prompt` and `fx_<domain>_spectacle_prompt` attach an effect to a ready scene, a person, a place or a stage. `scene_with_effect_prompt` and `fx_prompt` pick any. `fx_real_prompt` and `fx_spectacle_prompt` pick one tier.

Photographic effects that apply to a whole image (long exposure, haze, lens flare, motion blur, bokeh, light leaks, double exposure and more) are in `fx_photo_effect`, with `fx_photo_prompt` to use them on a landscape, city or product.

Extreme weather in 15 events (tornado, hurricane, blizzard, thunderstorm, hailstorm, flood, wildfire, drought, dust storm, ice storm, avalanche, tsunami, volcanic ash, monsoon, fog). Each event has matching sky, land, people, things, animals, plants and light files, so everything in one prompt belongs to the same storm.

Three layers. `wx_<event>_sky_prompt` is the sky and air, `wx_<event>_place_prompt` adds the effect on the land, and `wx_<event>_living_prompt` shows people, things, animals and plants. `wx_<event>_prompt` combines all three, and `wx_severity` gives mild, strong, severe and extreme.
Gallery sets. `wx_<event>_gallery_prompt` makes one image of four panels divided by thin white lines, showing the same place at the four severities. `wx_gallery_prompt` picks any event.

Each world has dress, props, setting and action files, such as `world_renaissance_props`, with every garment and object described in plain words. All are original archetypes with no named characters, franchises or brands.

short:
Every kind of adult, from every corner of the world, dressed in anything from a 5,000-year-old tunic to a plush hot-dog costume.

Guyanonymous' Wildcards gives your text-to-image prompts the whole world to draw from: more than 40,400 drop-in .txt files and 3.6 million lines covering adult characters of every age, body, ancestry and gender identity, plus garments and costumes from the Palaeolithic to today, accessories, footwear, makeup, tattoos, weapons, armour, surfboards and the places they stand in.

Most wildcard packs repeat the same faces, clothes and colours. Guyanonymous' Wildcards is built to do the opposite. It is a folder of plain .txt files that you drop into any wildcard-aware image tool and call with a name wrapped in double underscores. Build adult characters aged 18 to 120 with weighted bodies, hair, skin and clothing, or let one prompt pick a person in proportion to the world's adult population, by region or by country. Dress them from garment families that run from ballet to biker, flapper to festival, swimwear to formal wear, corsets to onesies; uniforms and costumes; 37 eras of dress; more than 35 accessory families; a full footwear system; and costumes for fursuiters, cosplayers, LARP and drag. Control sunburn and tan against each person's natural skin tone, dress them for any season or weather, add makeup, nails, piercings and body art, and set the scene in buildings, rooms and landscapes from every region. Everything is for making adult characters only, original wording, and written to embrace global diversity.
features:
- Whole-world characters. Adults aged 18 to 120 in nine age brackets, with weighted body types, hair, eyes, skin and clothing. One prompt can pick a person by real world population shares, by region or by country. Ethnicity lines now always state a skin colour that fits the group.

- Women's and men's sets. Matching female (f_) and male (m_) files, plus shared files, and demographic layers for cisgender, trans, non-binary, androgynous, intersex and individualized-transition identities, described by who people are.

- Garments. Families by type, era and subculture (about 560 files) with optional `_detail` versions that describe front, back, coverage and cut so the name is not doing all the work. Includes swimwear, lingerie, sleepwear, corsets, onesies, modest and revealing lines, and rave, festival and counterculture clothing.

- Uniforms and costumes. Hundreds of uniforms, ceremonial dress and cosplay archetypes, Halloween masks and costumes, and character costume for fursuit, cosplay, LARP, faire, reenactment, sci-fi, fantasy and drag.

- Accessories and footwear. More than 50 accessory families in six grades from basic to showpiece, about 430 shoe types, and assistive and adaptive items. Footwear now has quality files that run from cheap to absurdly expensive, with no prices. A `wardrobe_` index sorts items into worn dress, adornment and carried items.

- Body and skin. Makeup, nails, piercings, body art, tattoos and skin features, a clinical wound and injury overlay (`body_wound_*`, by severity and by category: puncture, fracture, burn, contagion, bite and sting, and more) with matching casts, splints and bandages (`acc_medwrap_*`), plus `skin_tan_*` files that apply a tan (faint to deepest) or sunburn (pink to blistered to peeling) in a way that is realistic for the person's natural skin tone.

- Condition. `condition_*` files describe any item's state, from pristine and brand new to old, worn, stained, marked and ruined, so they can be applied to anything in the library.

- Weather and seasons. 20 weather conditions with matching outfits, from heatwave to blizzard.

- Period dress. 37 eras from the Palaeolithic to the 2010s, mixing every region of the world.

- Objects, places and poses. Weapons of the world, armour, surfboards, 13 object families, buildings, rooms, landscapes, and solo and shared poses.

- Art, logos and style packs. Hundreds of original styles for images on objects, fictional logos and tattoos, plus illustration and photographic style packs.

- Two editions. The full weighted set, and an All Options Once edition with every option listed a single time.

- A library map. `docs/Library_Map.html` shows how the file names fit together and what each group adds.

- Adults only, original wording. No brands, no real people, no prices, and no minors in any prompt.
naming:
Version 36 unified the file names. A name now reads family, group, variant:

- `f_` / `m_`: female and male person files. Files with no prefix are shared.
- `age##_##_`: one layer per age bracket. `bt_`: body-type layers.
- `clothing_garment_`, `clothing_uniform_`, `clothing_onesie_`, `clothing_period_`: all clothing, under one prefix.
- `acc_<family>_`: accessories, with footwear as `acc_shoe_`. Tiers are `basic`, `standard`, `fine`, `luxury`, `showpiece` and `practical`.
- `costume_`: Halloween and character costume. `obj_`: objects, weapons, armour and surfboards.
- `body_`, `skin_tan_`, `tattoo_`: makeup, nails, piercings, tan and body art.
- `scene_`, `pose_`, `wx_`: places, poses and weather outfits. `world_` and `countries_`: people by region and country.
- `aoo_` in front of any name: the All Options Once edition.

If you used earlier versions, `filename_changes.txt` lists every old name and its new name. Some entry points changed: `__garment_prompt__` is now `__clothing_garment_prompt__`, and `__period_prompt__` is now `__clothing_period_prompt__`.
start:
1. Unzip and copy. Unzip Guyanonymous_Wildcards_v38.zip and copy the wildcards folder into your image tool's wildcard folder. Python is not needed to use it.

2. Call a file. Put the file name between double underscores in a prompt, for example `__f_prompt_master_by_age__` for a woman or `__m_prompt_master_by_age__` for a man.

3. Try a layer. Use `__world_person__` for a random person in world proportions, `__acc_prompt__` for an accessory, `__clothing_garment_prompt__` for a garment, `__clothing_period_prompt__` for period dress, `__wx_outfit_prompt__` for a weather outfit, or `__skin_tan_level__` for a tan or sunburn.

4. Mix and match. Combine them in one prompt, for example a person, then a garment, then an accessory. A blank line in any file means "none". `__v38_entry_points__` lists a starting file for each new section.

Optional: run `python3 tools/expand.py f_prompt_master_by_age` to preview sample prompts, and `python3 tools/build_all.py` to rebuild everything (about 10 to 15 minutes). The All Options Once edition uses the same names with an aoo_ prefix.
warning:
Many prompt files in this package are templates. Their lines contain references to other wildcard files, and those files can contain further references. A prompt can therefore be several layers deep, for example `__world_person__` calls a region file, which calls a country file, which calls the age, body and clothing files.

This can cause problems. If your image tool does not resolve nested wildcards fully, or stops at a fixed depth, some references may be left in the final prompt as raw text such as `__f_age25_34_prompt_char_face__` instead of being replaced. Check a few generated prompts before a big batch, and make sure your tool's wildcard depth or recursion setting is on.

To manage complex, layered prompts, the creator of this package uses [Offline Wildcard Prompt Studio](https://civitai.red/models/3016893/offline-wildcard-prompt-studio-v1), which works with any prompting system. It is a handy way to build and check nested prompts before you run them. The package also includes `python3 tools/expand.py` to preview prompts and `python3 tools/expand.py --check` to confirm every reference points to a real file.
